reason: 'semi-' is a hedge on glossy, like 'sub-' or '±'; the value is PATO_0001373 glistening (EXACT synonym glossy), marked approximate.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: A comparative of dull; like 'paler' and 'darker' in the previous review, it compares with an unstated part or surface. Plain 'dull' already has FLOPO:0991106.
Samaroid fruits and pods look like a samara (PO_0030099), whose defining feature is a flat wing; PATO_0104354 winged covers it. The 'does not split open' part of the meaning is not carried.
Same as rule C345 for 'taprooted': PO_0020127 primary root (EXACT synonym tap root) + present.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: rhomboid PATO_0001938 and elliptic PATO_0000947)
reason: A compound of two outline shapes that means a shape between them, the same as 'linear-lanceolate'; both values have terms.

A likeness to a part that is used on rhizomes, stems, roots and pseudobulbs, sometimes hedged ('nearly corm-like'). The nearest terms are PO_0025355 corm (its synonyms already include pseudobulb) and FLOPO:0991109 tuberous; neither fits closely enough to map, and a new 'corm-like' class is not justified by 16 mixed uses.
'Narrowly ovate' is ovate with a degree cue toward lanceolate; the outline value is FLOPO:0991024 ovate and the cue 'narrow' is lost.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: acute (sensu botany) FLOPO:0991095 and acuminate PATO_0002228)
reason: An apex shape between acute and acuminate, used in ranges ('acute-acuminate to caudate'); both values exist.
'Styles/carpels agglutinés les uns aux autres' = like parts stuck together without fusion: FLOPO:0991187 coherent.

target: new: conjunction of two values in one compound word (tuberculate FLOPO:0991060 and ciliated PATO_0001408)
reason: A margin or keel fringed with hairs that arise from tubercles; both values hold at once, so it is a conjunction, not a range between them. The flora pipeline already reads 'ciliate' as PATO_0001408.
Barbulate = minutely bearded (French 'barbues'; 'barbulate vein angles' = tufts of hairs in the vein axils): FLOPO:0991118 bearded. 'Ebarbulate' is its negation.

label: reduplicate
definition: A folded quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being folded lengthwise with its margins or halves turned outwards, so that in section it forms an inverted V. NOTE: Opposite of induplicate; sibling of FLOPO:0991123 conduplicate. Used of palm leaflets and of valvate aestivation with outturned edges.
reason: A standard botanical fold (palm leaves, aestivation) with no PATO or FLOPO term; PATO_0001910 folded is the right parent.
FLOPO:0991160 pedate is already defined as palmately divided with the lateral divisions divided again.

target: new: depth of division (split PATO_0001786 to a landmark: base, middle, midvein), approximate
reason: A fragment of 'divided nearly to the base/middle'; the content is how deep the split goes, which needs a landmark, not a term.
The examples mix several senses (sinuous thecae, twisted roots and wings, folded thallus) that are not PATO_0001966 convolute, an aestivation-like rolling; no single term fits.
FLOPO:0991152 loculicidal is the adjective of the same dehiscence ('déhiscence loculicide').

label: palmatipartite
definition: A split quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being cut more than halfway, but not fully, to the base into segments radiating from a common point. NOTE: Palmate counterpart of FLOPO:0991156 pinnatipartite; deeper than FLOPO:0991158 palmately lobed.
reason: Pinnatipartite has a FLOPO class but its palmate counterpart does not; 'palmately lobed' is shallower.

Most examples are a part stuck to a part of another kind (caruncle to seed, stem to substrate): FLOPO:0991188 adherent. 'Adhering to one another' (thecae, seeds in a mass) is better read as FLOPO:0991187 coherent.

Finger-like projections, lobes and pneumatophores are elongated, roughly cylindrical outgrowths; PATO_0001873 cylindrical is the nearest term. PATO_0001980 digitate means palmately compound, not finger-shaped. The blunt tip is not carried.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: mouth/orifice + increased width PATO_0000600)
reason: The quality belongs to the opening of the capsule, spur or pouch, not to the whole part; the value is increased width at that region.

target: new: conjunction of two values in one compound word (lanceolate PATO_0001877 and acuminate PATO_0002228)
reason: A lanceolate outline that ends in an acuminate tip: both values hold, one for the outline and one for the apex.
PATO_0002215 falciform has the EXACT synonyms hooked and uncinate ('non uncinées'); 'not hooked' is its negation.
Rootless / without roots / dépourvues de racines = complement of has_part some root, like 'awnless' and 'veinless'.
The negation of FLOPO:0991128 anastomosing, which inheres in the veins.
Soft-wooded = the wood is soft: PATO_0000387 soft inhering in secondary xylem (PO_0005848, synonym wood) of the stem or plant.
A mentum or connective drawn out like a spur ('prolongé en éperon'): PATO_0002540 spur shaped. A real spur on a petal or corolla is better read as the PO spur classes present.
Tape-like stipes, viscidia and petals are long, narrow and flat: PATO_0002430 strap-shaped.
All examples are about smell ('odeur désagréable'); FLOPO:0991020 foetid lists 'unpleasant smell' as a synonym.

target: new: conjunction of two values in one compound word (repand FLOPO:0991186 and dentated PATO_0001205)
reason: A shallowly wavy margin that also bears teeth; both values exist and hold together.
A relation to a named part ('enfolding the palea', 'enfolding the stem'); the second part is usually given, so it belongs in the relation pattern, not a term.
